It is a shikinaisha (small shrine), formerly ranked as a village shrine.

=== History ===
The deity {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}} is a son of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}. The shrine name is connected with traditions about descendants of this line and the "Shimada" surname.<ref>''Shinsen Shojiroku''.</ref>

From the late Heian period onward, ties with {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Q714559|qid=Q714559}} deepened. Together with other shikinaisha, it was invited to Kasuga's sacred mountain area and worshiped as one of four deities at Kasuga's Kii Shrine. Later records place the shrine at several locations around Yashima. In 1886, when the area of present Yashima Mausoleum was developed as Prince Sawara's mausoleum, the shrine and Sudo Tenno Shrine were moved and merged at the current site.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto
* Sudo Tenno ({{ill|Prince Sawara|Q1079634|qid=Q1079634}})

=== Precinct shrines ===
* Amaterasu Shrine - {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}}
* Kasuga Shrine - {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}} and Wa-no-shita Okami
* Small shrine enshrining Konjin

=== Main sanctuary ===
The honden is an old-style Kasuga-zukuri building (2.53 m x 1.92 m) with decorative metal fittings and a large porch. It is regarded as a transferred former Kasuga building ("Kasuga-utsushi"), later moved again at the time of merger in 1886. Different theories exist on the precise transfer date and original hall. It was designated a Nara City cultural property on March 1, 1982.

=== Stone lanterns ===
Because of the merger with Sudo Tenno Shrine, many lanterns bear inscriptions such as "Sudo Tenno" and "Yashima Tenno," including examples dated 1640, 1710, and 1754.
